Mad Catz Losses Jump, 37 Percent Of Staff To Be Laid Off On Weak Rock Band Hardware Sales (x-post /v/CoOpGaming)
I don't know what they expected - they keep trying to sell cheap, shitty peripherals at premium prices. They even managed to run the Saitek name in to the ground.

Yeah, the peripherals for Rock Band 4 are actually pretty solid and built better than Harmonix's previous games, but I think it's another case of "too little too late" and the fact that music games weren't the smash hit comeback that they might have anticipated.

As someone who bought rock band 4 I can say they're not even remotely worth the asking price. There were a number of problems with the launch - like price gouging those who bought the game digitally for the instruments. The guitar at launch was priced at $100 USD (stupid!) for the next gen systems on top of the $60 USD game. The older controllers for last-gen consoles would not work without a legacy adapter that was virtually impossible to find around here because no store stocked it.

The entire launch was a poorly planned cash grab, and it's no surprise it failed.

Yeah, the pricing is too high to sell well; I'm just talking about build quality. The previous guitar's strum bar felt too "squishy," and the drums felt more fragile that iteration. I like that they've got support for cymbals as an option, but I agree that the price for each piece is too high.

Why All Americans Should Support the Trans-Pacific Partnership: New at Reason

Utter nonsense. We are ardent traders (I like my cheap 3rd world products, so I'm even an ardent international trader), but the leap from supporting trade, or even international trade, to supporting the TPP is a leap I hope very few people are stupid enough to make.

This almost seems like a hoax.

First off, it's laughably illogical. It's really not even an actual defense of the TPP at all, since at no point does it get into the specifics of the TPP. It's actually just a defense of free trade, with the entirely unproven (and arguably undeserved) presumption that the two are equal and interchangeable.

Beyond that though - beyond the tortured illogic and empty rhetoric - it's terribly written. It's filled from end to end with labored, poorly constructed phrases and straightforward nonsense. It doesn't even begin to appear to be the work of professional writers. It actually reads as if it was a middle school student's current events paper.

Whether produced one city over, or on the other side of the world, imports are the sole purpose of our production.

What? Seriously, what the hell does "imports are the sole purpose of our production" even mean?

With trade, the focus is often understandably on the raise we all get for being open to the production of others.

"raise?" Was this even written by someone who speaks English? Was it machine-translated? Did they mean something akin to "increase?" The sentence as a whole would still be nonsense, but at least it would be more grammatically correct.

What this should remind us is that open borders to trade don’t impoverish us as much they’re the easily one of the quickest paths to much greater wealth.

"as much they're the easily one of the?" That's complete nonsense.

...and so on.

It's just... bizarre. It most certainly does not appear to be the considered opinion of any sort of reasonable thinkers OR the product of professional writers, but I'm not sure what it actually is, or is meant to be. It's too nonsensical to even serve as good propaganda.
